attributes.body_ja:
「なかなか」（漢字（かんじ）では「中々（なかなか）」）は、何（なに）かの程度（ていど）が思（おも）っていたよりも高（たか）いときに使（つか）われる副詞（ふくし）です。形容詞（けいようし）の前（まえ）や、名詞（めいし）と「の」の前（まえ）に置（お）いて使（つか）われます。

「なかなか」は、その対象（たいしょう）を「軽（かる）く見（み）ることができない」や「無視（むし）できない」のようなニュアンスを持（も）つ場合（ばあい）もあります。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「なかなか」のニュアンスを、ダーツの的（まと）を使（つか）って考（かんが）えてみましょう。まずは、的（まと）全体（ぜんたい）があるものの程度（ていど）を示（しめ）しているとイメージしてみてください。「なかなか」が使（つか）われるのは、想像（そうぞう）を超（こ）えて、ダーツがその的（まと）の真（ま）ん中（なか）に近（ちか）いところに当（あ）たったようなときです。このように、「なかなか」は思（おも）っていたよりも程度（ていど）が高（たか）いとき、期待（きたい）以上（いじょう）であるときに使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「なかなか」は、漢字（かんじ）で書（か）くと「中々（なかなか）」になります。
attributes.body:
なかなか (or 中々（なかなか） in kanji) is an adverb in Japanese that is frequently translated as 'very', or 'considerably'. It is regularly paired directly with other adjectives, or before nouns (with の coming between なかなか and the noun).

なかなか can also sometimes have the nuance of being something that is 軽視（けいし）しがたい. This basically translates as 'difficult to dismiss', but is a bit closer to English expressions like 'nothing to scoff at', or 'not to be taken lightly'.

Fun Fact

なかなか highlights that something is 'considerably/extremely (A)', or 'far more (A) than expected'. If we imagine a dartboard, where the whole board shows the intensity level of a specific word, and なかなか represents the bullseye, this is basically the nuance. '(A) is the middle (bullseye) example of (B)'.

Fun Fact

なかなか, coming from the kanji 中（なか） meaning 'within', can be thought to mean the 'middle' or 'most' (A).

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: How to use なかなか

attributes.body: Both なかなか and けっこう are adverbs used to express extent. In affirmative sentences, they can both mean 'quite' or 'rather.' A key difference is that なかなか is often used in negative sentences to express difficulty in doing something. Meanwhile, けっこう can be used alone (especially as けっこうです) to politely decline something, like saying 'I'm fine.'

なかなか means 'quite' or 'fairly' when used with positive expressions, e.g. なかなか面白い映画だった ('It was quite an interesting movie.') In contrast, なかなか～ない expresses difficulty or delay, meaning 'not easily' or 'hardly', e.g. 仕事がなかなか終わらない ('The work just won't end.')

second_relatable.title: なかなか～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not really, Hardly, Not easily or readily, By no means, Far from

attributes.body: Both express degree, but with different implications. なかなか implies something is quite or unexpectedly good, e.g. なかなかいい店だね ('This place is surprisingly good.') あまり highlights an excessive degree that leads to an unintended or negative result, e.g. 緊張のあまり声が震えた ('I was so nervous my voice shook.')

なかなか and あまり～ない both express degree, but in opposite directions. なかなか implies exceeding expectations, e.g. なかなか美味しい ('It's quite tasty.'). In contrast, あまり～ない suggests a lesser degree, or falling short of expectations, e.g. あまり美味しくない ('It's not very tasty.').

second_relatable.title: あまり～ない
second_relatable.meaning: Not very, Not much, Not really, Hardly

attributes.body: Though both contain なか, their meanings are different. なかなか is often used in negatives to express difficulty, like 'not easily' (なかなかできません), or in positives to mean 'quite' (なかなかいい). In contrast, のなかで means 'among' and is used when referring to one or more members of a group. For example, 果物の中でりんごが一番好き means 'Among fruits, I like apples the best.'.

Both emphasize degree, but differ in nuance. なかなか suggests something is quite or surprisingly so, often with a positive tone, e.g. なかなか面白い映画だった ('It was quite an interesting movie.') あまりに means 'too much' or 'excessively', and is often negative in tone, e.g. あまりに寒くて出かけられなかった ('It was too cold to go out.')

When used in affirmative sentences, なかなか and かなり both convey the nuance that something exceeds expectations, e.g. なかなか美味しい ('It's quite tasty.') or かなり美味しい (essentially the same meaning). The main difference is that なかなか is often used in negative expressions to suggest that something is not easily done, e.g. なかなかうまくいかない ('It just won't go well.'), while かなり is not used this way.
